content:
Bloomberg reported today that Apple is about to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" hardware rental programme. Users can subscribe to new Apple products on a monthly fee basis, but according to reports, the programme has a restriction that we hope will not materialise in the end.

The "Apple Upgrade" is said to make higher-priced products more accessible, but entry-level models are not included

Due to the ongoing AI-driven memory chip shortage, most Apple products have recently seen price increases.

As autumn approaches, this trend is expected to intensify further, with new iPhone and Apple Watch models also predicted to become more expensive. Not to mention the upcoming higher-end iPhone Ultra and MacBook Ultra products.

According to Mark Gurman, Apple's response is to launch a brand-new monthly subscription rental option for hardware.

Gurman said this option will debut next week on Apple's online store and retail outlets first.

Before the final details are set in stone, I believe that making Apple products more affordable in this way is a good move.

Apple Upgrade will be entirely voluntary, so any user who wishes to purchase a product outright can still do so as usual. Especially amid the recent wave of price hikes, adding more options should be a natural course of action.

My only concern relates to eligible hardware. Gurman noted that some devices will not be eligible for Apple Upgrade, including "the Apple Watch SE, entry-level iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo".

It would be a shame if Apple does not allow users to purchase its most affordable products through the rental programme.

Just imagine: you always thought Apple products were out of reach, but thanks to this new programme, you could own a MacBook Neo for just US$20 a month. In this case, Apple Upgrade has the potential to bring a flood of new users to the Apple ecosystem.

I understand Apple's desire to use this to steer users towards higher-priced products, but restricting Apple Upgrade to specific hardware feels like an unnecessary move and would limit the programme's impact.

What are your thoughts on the reported Apple Upgrade programme? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
